cards.title: Model Validation and Diagnostic Criteria
cards.claim: Model validation is critical and requires multiple methods. Goodness-of-fit (GOF) plots (DV vs IPRED/xPRED, residuals vs predictions/time) and simulation-based diagnostics (VPC, pcVPC, NPC, NPDE) are used. High shrinkage obscures EBE-based diagnostics, making simulation-based checks more informative. External validation uses data not used for model building.
conditions: No single validation method is sufficient.
Shrinkage >20-30% limits utility of individual diagnostics.
External validation requires data excluded from model development; independent studies or a predeclared held-out set may supply them.
limitations: Internal validation relies on the same data used for building.
Data splitting reduces power to detect covariates.
Shrinkage affects reliability of individual post-hoc estimates.
cards.downstream_use: Qualifying models for regulatory submission or internal decision-making; assessing model robustness.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
